I​NTERVENOR​​REBECCA​​BURNETT’S​​CLOSING​​BRIEF​
 ​Comes​​now​​Rebecca​​Burnett,​​Intervenor​​and​​affected​​landowner,​​appearing​​pro​​se,​​and​
  ​files​​this​​Closing​​Brief​​in​​the​​above-referenced​​contested​​case​​proceeding​​and​​respectfully​
   ​shows​​as​​follows:​

                                         ​I.​​INTRODUCTION​​AND​​STATEMENT​​OF​​THE​​CASE​
I​ntervenor​​Rebecca​​Burnett​​is​​the​​heir​​of​​approximately​​104​​acres​​of​​land​​located​​in​​Bell​
 ​County,​​Texas.​ ​Proposed​​route​​segment/link​​A2​​as​​filed​​by​​the​​Applicants​​LCRA​​Transmission​
  ​Services​​Corporation(LCRA​​TSC)​​and​​Oncor​​Electric​​Delivery​​Company​​LLC(ONCOR)​​crosses​
   ​Intervenor’s​​property​​for​​approximately​​2,100​​linear​​feet,​​traversing​​improved​​pastures,​​native​
    ​type​​rangeland,cultivated​​land(interseeded,​​drilled​​forages),creek​​bottom(Glass​​Branch)​ ​all​​of​
     ​which​​is​​either​​temporarily​​or​​permanently​​cross-fenced​​within​​substantial​​boundary​​fencing​
      ​within​​our​​property.​
       ​Intervenor​​timely​​intervened​​in​​this​​proceeding​​and​​submitted​​direct​​testimony​​filed​​on​​the​​PUC​
        ​Interchange​​at​​item​​Number​​5472.​​The​​Hearing​​on​​Merits​​was​​conducted​​June​​8​​through​
         ​12,2026.​​This​​Closing​​Brief​​is​​submitted​​pursuant​​to​​the​​SOAH​​Order​​governing​​post-hearing​
          ​Briefing​​and​​is​​filed​​in​​accordance​​with​​the​​June​​19,2026​​deadline​​established​​by​​the​
           ​Administrative​​Law​​Judge.​

I​nternenor​​respectfully​​urges​​the​​Administrative​​Law​​Judge​​to​​recommend​​to​​the​​Public​​Utility​
 ​Commission​​of​​Texas(PUC​​or​​Commission)​​that​​the​​proposed​​route​​segment/link​​crossing​
  ​or​​adjacent​​to​​intervenor’s​​property​​not​​be​​selected,​​and​​that​​the​​Commission​​instead​​approve​
   ​an​​alternative​​route​​or​​combination​​of​​route​​segments/links​​that​​avoids​​the​​Intervenor’s​
    ​property​​or​​materially​​reduces​​adverse​​impacts​​upon​​it.​

                                    ​II.PROPOSED​​FINDINGS​​OF​​FACT​

I​ntervenor​​proposes​​the​​following​​findings​​of​​fact,​​each​​of​​which​​is​​supported​​by​​evidence​​in​​the​
 ​record.​​Exhibit​​and​​transcript​​citations​​should​​be​​inserted​​at​​the​​bracketed​​references.​
  ​1.Intervenor​​Rebecca​​Burnett​​is​​heir​​to​​104​​acres​​located​​on​​tracts​​3502​​and​​3503​​as​​identified​
   ​by​​the​​Applicants​​in​​Bell​​County,​​Texas.[Cite:Intervenor’s​​Direct​​Testimony]​
    ​2.Proposed​​Route​​using​​Segment/Link​​A2​​would​​cross​​Intervenor’s​​property​​for​​approximately​
     ​2,100​​linear​​feet,​​entering​​at​​front​​of​​property​​along​​US​​Highway​​190​​and​​then​​bisecting​​the​
      ​Intervenor’s​​tracts​​3502​​and​​3503​​at​​a​​diagonal​​and​​exiting​​the​​Intervenor’s​​property​​on​​the​​west​
       ​side​​toward​​the​​back​​of​​the​​Intervenor’s​​property.[Cite:​​Intervenor’s​​Direct​​Testimony,​​Bruce​
        ​Burnett’s​​Direct​​Testimony;​​Applicant’s​​Testimony.]​
         ​3.The​​crossing​​onto​​our​​property​​if​​this​​proposed​​765kv​​transmission​​line​​is​​built​​would​​bisect​
          ​and​​fragment​​the​​Intervenor’s​​improved​​pasture,​​native​​pasture,​​creek/bottomland(Glass​
           ​Branch)​​and​​make​​our​​104​​acres​​of​​ranchland​​difficult​​or​​impossible​​to​​use​​as​​intended.​
            ​[Cite:​​Intervenor’s​​Direct​​Testimony;​​Bruce​​Burnett’s​​Direct​​Testimony.]​
             ​4.The​​proposed​​route​​using​​segment/link​​A2​​crosses​​our​​creek(Glass​​Branch)​​known​​by​​the​
              ​family​​and​​having​​appeared​​on​​Txdot​​maps.​​[Cite:Intervenor’s​​Direct​​Testimony;​​Bruce​​Burnett’s​
               ​Direct​​Testimony.]​
                ​5.Alternative​​routes​​using​​Segment/Link​​A3​​would​​achieve​​the​​same​​transmission​​objectives​​as​
                 ​the​​Applicant’s​​preferred​​routing​​while​​avoiding​​the​​Intervenor’s​​property​​entirely.​
                  ​[Cite:Applicant’s​​Environmental​​Assessment​​in​​the​​Application​​as​​filed​​on​​the​​Interchange.]​

                                    ​III.PROPOSED​​CONCLUSIONS​​OF​​LAW​

    ​1.​ ​The​​PUC​​has​​jurisdiction​​over​​this​​proceeding​​pursuant​​to​​Texas​​Utilities​​Code​​Sections​
                   ​37.051​​and​​37056​​.​
     ​2.​ ​The​​applicable​​standard​​for​​approval​​of​​a​​CCN​​for​​a​​new​​transmission​​line​​is​​governed​
                    ​By​​Texas​​Utilities​​Code​​Section​​37.056(c)​​,​​which​​directs​​the​​Commission​​to​​consider:​
           ​(a)the​​adverse​​effects​​on​​the​​scenic,aesthetic​​and​​recreational​​value​​of​​the​​surrounding​
            ​area;(b)the​​effects​​on​​the​​natural​​environment,​​historic​​sites​​and​​areas​​of​​particular​
             ​environmental​​concern;(c)the​​effects​​on​​vegetation,water,fish​​and​​wildlife;(d)whether​​the​
              ​route​​utilizes​​existing​​compatible​​rights-of-way;(e)the​​effects​​on​​residential​​and​
               ​commercial​​development;(f)whether​​the​​route​​conforms​​with​​the​​policy​​of​​prudent​
                ​avoidance​​and(g)community​​values,​​recreational​​and​​park​​areas,​​historical​​and​​aesthetic​
                 ​values,environmental​​integrity​​and​ ​the​​probable​​improvement​​of​​service​​or​​lowering​​of​
                  ​Cost​​to​​consumers​​in​​the​​area.​

    ​3.​ ​The​​Commission​​is​​not​​required​​to​​approve​​any​​particular​​route​​segment/link​​proposed​
            ​By​​the​​Applicants.​ ​All​​122​​alternative​​routes​​and​​route​​links​​included​​in​​the​​CCN​
             ​Application​​are​​available​​for​​selection​​and​​approval​​by​​the​​PUC.​
              ​[See​​CCN​​Application​​-March​​26,2026.]​
     ​4.​ ​The​​evidence​​in​​this​​record​​does​​not​​support​​approval​​of​​Route​​Segment/Link​​A2​​as​
                              ​The​​preferred​​routing​​across​​Intervenor’s​​property(tracts​​3502,3503)​​because​​the​
               ​proposed765kv​​transmission​​line​​would​​be​​close​​to​​our​​working​​pens(steel​​pipe)​​and​
                               ​Our​​dry​​cabin​​as​​well​​as​​our​​creek(Glass​​Branch)​​creating​​problems/issues​​for​
                ​our​​operation.​​The​​segment​​would​​diagonally​​cross​​and​​bisect​​our​​property​​for​
                 ​approximately​​2,100​​linear​​feet​​in​​two​​of​​our​​largest​​pastures​​and​​fields​​we​​plant​​forage​
                  ​in​​twice​​a​​year.​​This​​transmission​​line​​would​​make​​access​​and​​utilization​​of​​our​​property​
                   ​very​​difficult​​if​​not​​impossible.​​[Cite:​​Intervenor’s​​Direct​​Testimony,​​Bruce​​Burnett’s​​Direct​
                    ​Testimony.]​
      ​5.​ ​An​​alternative​​route​​or​​combination​​of​​route​​segments/links​​is​​available​​in​​the​​record​
                     ​That​​better​​satisfies​​the​​factors​​set​​forth​​in​​Texas​​Utilities​​Code​​Section​​37.056(c)​​as​
                      ​Applied​​to​​the​​corridor​​traversing​​Intervenor’s​​property.​

                                      ​IV.​​ARGUMENT​




        ​A.The​​Statutory​​Factors​​Weigh​​Against​​Selection​​of​​Route​​A2​​Across​​Intervenor’s​
             ​Property​
              ​Texas​​Utilities​​Code​​Section​​37.056(c)​​sets​​forth​​the​​factors​​the​​Commission​​must​
               ​weigh​​in​​selecting​​a​​CCN​​route.​​The​​evidence​​introduced​​at​​the​​Hearing​​on​​the​​Merits​
                ​Demonstrates​​that​​several​​of​​these​​factors​​weigh​​against​​the​​selection​​of​
                 ​Segment/Link​​A2​​as​​the​​route​​crossing​​Intervenor’s​​property.​
         ​1.Community​​Values,Aesthetic​​Values​​and​​Effects​​on​​Residential​​Development​
                  ​Segment/Link​​A2​​would​​place​​a​​765kv​​Transmission​​Line​​in​​our​​properties​​boundaries​
                   ​for​​about​​2,100​​linear​​feet​​bisecting​​and​​fragmenting​​(tracts​​3502,3503)​​our​​two​
                    ​Largest​​pastures​​and​​this​​would​​alter​​the​​character​​of​​our​​ranch.​​Our​​family​​having​
                     ​farmed​​and​​ranched​​this​​land​​for​​over​​seventy​​years.​​These​​proposed​​765kv​
                      ​transmission​​lines​​would​​have​​towers​​165’​​to​​200’​​tall​​filling​​a​​200’​​wide​​easement​
                        ​And​​will​​detrimentally​​affect​​the​​rural​​community​​values​​our​​family​​and​​our​​neighbors​
                         ​Expect.​​This​​transmission​​line​​implicates​​both​​the​​community​​values​​and​​prudent​
                          ​Avoidance​​policy​​in​​Section​​37.056(c).[Intervenor’s​​Testimony,​​Bruce​​Burnett​
​Testimony.]​
          ​Rebecca​​Burnett​​Closing​​Brief​ ​page​​3​​of​​5​
 ​PUC​​Docket​​No.​​59475​          ​SOAH​​Docket​​No.​​473-26-16349​


​2.Availability​​of​​Existing​​or​​Compatible​​Rights-of-Way​
   ​Alternative​​Segment​​A3​​is​​in​​very​​close​​proximity​​to​​existing​​industrial​​operations​​and​
    ​facilities​​including​​solar​​farms,​​electrical​​substations,​​transmission​​lines​​and​​battery​
     ​electric​​storage​​facilities.​​Our​​property(tracts​​3502​​and​​3503)​​do​​not​​have​​any​
      ​encumbered​​rights-of-way​​at​​this​​point​​in​​time.​
       ​[Cite:​​Intervenor’s​​Direct​​Testimony;​​Bruce​​Burnett’s​​Direct​​Testimony;​
         ​Applicant’s​​CCN​​Application​​and​​associated​​maps.]​

​B.​​Applicants​​Did​​Not​​Demonstrate​​That​​Segment​​A2​​Is​​Superior​​To​​Available​
               ​Alternatives​​On​​The​​Statutory​​Factors​
 ​The​​burden​​in​​a​​CCN​​proceeding​​rests​​with​​the​​Applicants​​to​​demonstrate​​that​​their​
  ​proposed​​route​​satisfies​​the​​statutory​​criteria.​ ​In​​this​​proceeding,​​Applicants​​introduced​
   ​an​​environmental​​Assessment​​ranking​​122​​alternative​​routes​​across​​multiple​​criteria.​
    ​However,​​the​​evidence​​does​​not​​establish​​that​​Segment​​A2​​is​​preferred​​over​​available​
     ​alternatives​​on​​the​​factors​​most​​directly​​applicable​​in​​Intervenor’s​​property.​​The​​revised​
      ​Route​​including​​segment/link​​A3​​seems​​superior​​as​​it​​routes​​through​​a​​part​
           ​of​​the​​county​​that​​is​​disturbed​​and​​occupied​​by​​transmission​​line​​rights-of-way,​​solar​
       ​farms,​​electrical​​substations​​and​​battery​​electric​​storage​​facilities​​making​​the​​area​​at​​and​
        ​adjacent​​to​​A3​​an​​industrial​​park​​or​​area​​as​​opposed​​to​​a​​strictly​​rural​​and​​ranchland​
         ​Inhabited​​area.​​[See:​​Intervenor’s​​Direct​​Testimony;​​Bruce​​Burnett​​Direct​​Testimony;​
          ​Applicants​​Direct​​Testimony;​​Applicants​​Appendix​​C,​​page​​C-47.Figure​​6-29.]​

​C.​​The​​PUC​​Has​​Full​​Authority​​To​​Select​​An​​Alternative​​Segment​​and​​Should​
                   ​Exercise​​That​​Authority​​Here.​
 ​The​​CCN​​Application​​filed​​March​​26,2026​​includes​​data​​on​​122​​alternative​​routes​​and​
  ​all​​those​​routes​​and​​route​​links​​are​​available​​for​​selection​​and​​approval​​by​​the​​PUC.​
   ​The​​Commission​​is​​not​​constrained​​to​​approve​​any​​particular​​route​​or​​combination​
    ​proposed​​by​​Applicants.​ ​The​​selection​​of​​the​​final​​route​​rests​​with​​the​​Commission​
     ​following​​its​​review​​of​​the​​ALJ’s​​Proposal​​For​​Decision.​​Intervenor​​respectfully​​submits​
      ​that​​Route​​Segment/Link​​A3​​or​​a​​combination​​thereof​​would​​satisfy​​the​​statutory​​factors​
       ​of​​Texas​​Utilities​​Code​​Section​​37.056(c)​​while​​meaningfully​​reducing​​the​​burden​
        ​Imposed​​on​​Intervenor’s​​property.​​Segment/Link​​A3​​would​​place​​the​​route​​in​​an​​already​
         ​Industrialized​​area/corridor​​of​​the​​county​​while​​maintaining​​the​​Intervenor’s​​property​
          ​as​​rural​​ranch/farmland.​​Segment/Link​​A3​​would​​not​​significantly​​increase​​costs​​or​
           ​Overall​​length​​and​​would​​certainly​​avoid​​creating​​new​​rights-of-way​​onto​​the​​Intervenor’s​
            ​Property​​as​​well​​as​​avoiding​​more​​habitable​​structures.​ ​Adoption​​of​​this​​alternative​
             ​Is​​consistent​​with​​the​​Commission’s​​obligation​​to​​weigh​​all​​of​​the​​Section​​37.056c​

             ​Large​​properties,​​then​​yes.”​ ​I​​surely​​felt​​this​​statement/​​reply​​by​​Smitherman​​does​
              ​especially​​apply​​to​​our​​property.[Mr.​​Smitherman​​Testimony​​from​​June​​11,2026​​on​​Page​

                       I. INTRODUCTION AND STATEMENT OF THE CASE
Intervenor Rebecca Burnett is the heir of approximately 104 acres of land located in Bell
County, Texas. Proposed route segment/link A2 as filed by the Applicants LCRA Transmission
Services Corporation(LCRA TSC) and Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC(ONCOR) crosses
Intervenor's property for approximately 2,100 linear feet, traversing improved pastures, native
type rangeland,cultivated land(interseeded, drilled forages),creek bottom(Glass Branch) all of
which is either temporarily or permanently cross-fenced within substantial boundary fencing
within our property.
Intervenor timely intervened in this proceeding and submitted direct testimony filed on the PUC
Interchange at item Number 5472. The Hearing on Merits was conducted June 8 through
12,2026. This Closing Brief is submitted pursuant to the SOAH Order governing post-hearing
Briefing and is filed in accordance with the June 19,2026 deadline established by the
Administrative Law Judge.

Internenor respectfully urges the Administrative Law Judge to recommend to the Public Utility
Commission of Texas(PUC or Commission) that the proposed route segment/link crossing
or adjacent to intervenor's property not be selected, and that the Commission instead approve
an alternative route or combination of route segments/links that avoids the Intervenor's
property or materially reduces adverse impacts upon it.

                             Il.PROPOSED FINDINGS OF FACT

Intervenor proposes the following findings of fact, each of which is supported by evidence in the
record. Exhibit and transcript citations should be inserted at the bracketed references.
1.Intervenor Rebecca Burnett is heir to 104 acres located on tracts 3502 and 3503 as identified
by the Applicants in Bell County, Texas.[Cite:Intervenor's Direct Testimony]
2.Proposed Route using Segment/Link A2 would cross Intervenor's property for approximately
2,100 linear feet, entering at front of property along US Highway 190 and then bisecting the
Intervenor's tracts 3502 and 3503 at a diagonal and exiting the Intervenor's property on the west
side toward the back of the Intervenor's property.[Cite: Intervenor's Direct Testimony, Bruce
Burnett's Direct Testimony; Applicant's Testimony.]
3.The crossing onto our property if this proposed 765kv transmission line is built would bisect
and fragment the Intervenor's improved pasture, native pasture, creek/bottomland(Glass
Branch) and make our 104 acres of ranchland difficult or impossible to use as intended.
[Cite: Intervenor's Direct Testimony; Bruce Burnett's Direct Testimony.]
4.The proposed route using segment/link A2 crosses our creek(Glass Branch) known by the
